summary: What a provider plugin says beside a failure of class `blocked`: the provider refused this call for a reason outside the work item and did nothing for it — money, a reached limit, a revoked credential or a broken channel — so a repeat once the block clears is a first act. The binding is the one the attempt ran under; the human-readable detail is the failure's own message.

scope.description: What is blocked: `account`, every call through this binding; `sender`, one sending account under it, such as a mailbox that reached its daily limit.

sender_external_id.description: The provider's identifier of the sending account that is blocked, as the operation's arguments name a sender. Present exactly when the scope is `sender`.

reason.description: Why, in the contract's words: `billing` (credits, a plan, a subscription or a payment), `limit` (an allowance the provider counts), `credential` (a key or a sign-in the provider no longer accepts), `channel` (a mailbox or a social account disconnected or paused), `other` where none of these fits.

link.description: Where a person goes to clear it, as the provider gave it: an https address.

clears_at.description: When the provider says the block clears by itself, such as an allowance that renews. Absent where the provider did not say; a hint, never the only way the block is known to have cleared.
